entries.clue: Cut the woman's slinky move! (7)

blocks.note: a slit is a cut
the woman's thing is hers: HER

annotation.surface: A woman's sinuous dance step gets snipped out of the routine.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cut" looks like an order to remove something, but it is simply the first noun of the build.
annotation.definitionFit: A slither is a smooth, sliding, snake-like movement, which is exactly a slinky move.

entries.clue: Start to screw royal to cut the ice, so to speak (5)

annotation.definition: cut the ice, so to speak

indicatorNotes.Start to: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of screw
Kate, Princess of Wales, is a royal

annotation.surface: A cheeky suggestion about a member of the royal family, dressed up as breaking the ice.
annotation.walkthrough: The Private Eye tone makes "screw royal" look like the sense, but only its S is used; "so to speak" flags that skating literally cuts ice.
annotation.definitionFit: A skater's blades carve lines in the ice, so to skate is, jokily, to cut the ice.

entries.clue: One resistance soldier not giving a shit routinely? (9)

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a regular is a soldier in the standing army

annotation.surface: A member of the resistance who is constipated, or who just doesn't care about routine.
annotation.walkthrough: An irregular is also a guerrilla fighter, so the surface's resistance soldier is the answer too; the question mark admits the lavatory joke in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who does not go to the toilet on a regular schedule is, in the medical sense, irregular.

entries.clue: Bit of thigh and rest's disturbed, pet? (7)

indicatorNotes.disturbed: disturbed letters are knocked out of their order

blocks.note: the ham is the back of the thigh
REST rearranged; the 's stands for is

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a pet has been sleeping badly on their leg.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as is: rest is disturbed. HAM for the back of the thigh is the root of hamstring.
annotation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small rodent kept as a pet.

entries.clue: Bishop's dropped from office – source of beef? (5)

indicatorNotes.dropped from: something dropped from a word is taken out of it

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a local branch is an office of a bank or firm

annotation.surface: A bishop leaves his office and someone asks what the grievance was about.
annotation.walkthrough: "Beef" hints at a complaint; the question mark says it is the cattle kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A ranch raises beef cattle, so it is where beef comes from.

entries.clue: Goodness comes from a lot of money, money initially lacking (5)

indicatorNotes.initially lacking: lacking its initial letter, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: G is a grand, a thousand pounds
LOLLY, slang for money, without its L

annotation.surface: A moralising line that virtue comes from wealth.
annotation.walkthrough: "Goodness" poses as virtue, but it is the mild exclamation. Lolly is British slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: "Goodness!" and "Golly!" are interchangeable mild exclamations of surprise.

entries.clue: Great to admit it's a big 'un (5-2)

blocks.note: gr. is an abbreviation for great
to own up is to admit

annotation.surface: Someone is urged to confess that something is very large.
annotation.walkthrough: "Admit" looks like a container instruction, but OWN UP simply follows GR.
annotation.definitionFit: Children call an adult a grown-up or a big 'un.

entries.clue: Solitary unit between political extremes? (5)

indicatorNotes.between: a piece placed between two others sits inside them

blocks.note: left and right, the two ends of the political spectrum
one is the unit

annotation.surface: A lone centrist is squeezed between the far left and the far right.
annotation.walkthrough: The political extremes are the letters L and R, the left and right ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A solitary, as a noun, is a person who lives alone: a loner.

entries.clue: see 15dn. (3)
City: "Cameron's at variance" (10)

indicatorNotes.variance: letters at variance disagree with their order

blocks.note: CAMERONSAT rearranged

annotation.surface: A headline quoting David Cameron as being at odds with a city.
annotation.walkthrough: The AT of "at variance" is part of the letters; only "variance" instructs.
annotation.definitionFit: Sacramento is a city, the state capital of California.

entries.clue: see 28dn.
Crew relieving wife from burden (5)

indicatorNotes.relieving: to relieve a burden of something is to take it off
indicatorNotes.from: says which word loses the letter

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a weight is a burden

annotation.surface: A household crew takes the load off the wife.
annotation.walkthrough: A rowing eight is the crew of eight oarsmen, so "Crew" is the definition, not a group of helpers.
annotation.definitionFit: In rowing, an eight is a boat and its crew of eight rowers.

entries.clue: Under-performing during hot date causing division (7)

indicatorNotes.performing: letters performing are doing a turn, rearranged
indicatorNotes.during: one thing during another sits inside it

blocks.note: H for hot, as on a tap
UNDER rearranged
D is the abbreviation for date

annotation.surface: Someone who fails in bed on a hot date and the couple split up.
annotation.walkthrough: "Under-performing" reads as one word but splits into fodder and instruction. A hundred is an old subdivision of an English county.
annotation.definitionFit: A hundred was an administrative division of a shire in England.

entries.clue: China was the first to back capitalist newspaper (5)

indicatorNotes.to back: sent back, the word reads right to left

blocks.note: whoever was first led
the Financial Times, the City's paper

annotation.surface: China is credited with being first to support a business paper.
annotation.walkthrough: "China" is the pottery, not the country.
annotation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of Delft, a kind of china.

entries.clue: NRA could after shifting pot (8)

indicatorNotes.after shifting: the letters as they stand after being shifted about

blocks.note: NRACOULD rearranged

annotation.surface: The US gun lobby wonders what it might do after moving marijuana.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pot" suggests cannabis in a surface about American politics; it is the cooking kind. The NRA is the National Rifle Association.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cauldron is the big iron pot hung over a fire, the witches' kind.

entries.clue: Trick action misfired – missing a ball (5)

indicatorNotes.misfired: a misfired word has its letters go off wrongly
indicatorNotes.missing: missing means that letter is taken out

blocks.note: ACTION without an O
O is round like a ball

annotation.surface: A sporting trick shot goes wrong and misses the ball.
annotation.walkthrough: The letter O stands for a ball because of its shape.
annotation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful trick or caper, usually heard as antics.

entries.clue: (& 7dn.) Tony's lost the plot finally? So far, no (3)

indicatorNotes.lost: someone lost has gone astray, so the letters wander
indicatorNotes.finally: takes the final letter of each word

blocks.note: taken as it stands
final letters of the and plot

annotation.surface: Has Tony Blair gone mad? Not so far.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer continues into 7 down. "Lost the plot" is an idiom for going crazy, but only "lost" instructs.
annotation.definitionFit: "Not yet" means that something has not happened so far.

entries.clue: Rubbish females breaking into store (6)

indicatorNotes.breaking into: a burglar breaking into a place ends up inside it

blocks.note: a pile is a stored heap
F for female, doubled for the plural

annotation.surface: Nonsense about women burgling a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: Doubling a letter makes the plural, as FF for females, like pp for pages.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the nonsense sense: calling someone's talk piffle dismisses it as rubbish.

entries.clue: Ignored, in disbelief – or got tense (9)

blocks.note: the F of the expletive blurted in disbelief, as in WTF
taken as it stands
gotten is a past tense form of got

annotation.surface: Someone hears they have been overlooked and reacts with disbelief and nerves.
annotation.walkthrough: "Got tense" looks like nervousness, but it asks for another form of the verb: GOTTEN, the American and old British past participle.
annotation.definitionFit: Something ignored has been forgotten, left out of mind.

entries.clue: Having erection after can cause trouble (4,2)

blocks.note: can and stir are both slang for prison
something erect is up

annotation.surface: An arousal-related mishap in the loo that leads to embarrassment.
annotation.walkthrough: "Can" is a toilet in the surface but British prison slang in the wordplay, as is stir; "after" fixes the order.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: you stir up trouble the way you stir a pot, making things churn.

entries.clue: Action: corpses everywhere (7)

indicatorNotes.everywhere: letters everywhere are scattered all over

blocks.note: CORPSES rearranged

annotation.surface: A film director's call to action on a set littered with bodies.
annotation.walkthrough: "Action" is the lawsuit sense, not the director's call.
annotation.definitionFit: In law a process is a legal action or the writ that starts one.

entries.clue: Still flipping crushing virtue? Sheer recklessness! (8)

indicatorNotes.flipping: flipped over, the word reads backwards
indicatorNotes.crushing: one piece crushing another holds it squeezed inside

blocks.note: still and yet both mean nevertheless
merit is a virtue

annotation.surface: An exasperated cry at someone still stamping all over decency.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flipping" reads as a mild British swear word, but it is the instruction to turn YET round.
annotation.definitionFit: Temerity is rash boldness, reckless audacity.

entries.clue: Have sex, wrapping chain on top of erect chopper (7)

indicatorNotes.wrapping: a wrapper goes round what it holds
indicatorNotes.top of: the top of a down word is its first letter

blocks.note: animals mate
ch. is the abbreviation for chain, a surveyor's measure
first letter of erect

annotation.surface: A saucy line about sex, a chain and an erect chopper.
annotation.walkthrough: "Chopper" is slang for penis in the surface; the definition is the cutting tool. "On" adds E after CH inside the wrap.
annotation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife for chopping, a chopper.

entries.clue: City centre's gone (Conservative cuts) – that'll do for me (7)

indicatorNotes.centre's gone: the middle of the word is removed

blocks.note: CITY without its central IT
C for Conservative
to lop is to cut

annotation.surface: A voter complains the city has been hollowed out by Tory cuts and they've had enough.
annotation.walkthrough: "Me" is the setter, Cyclops, whose name the clue signs off with.
annotation.definitionFit: The setter is Cyclops, so the name is what will do for "me".

entries.clue: Cringe about Bercow going topless (5)

indicatorNotes.about: brought about, the letters turn round so the end comes to the front
indicatorNotes.going topless: the top letter of a down word goes

blocks.note: BERCOW without its B

annotation.surface: Squirming at the thought of the former Speaker John Bercow stripping off.
annotation.walkthrough: John Bercow was Speaker of the House of Commons. ERCOW rotates its last three letters to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe shrinking back in fear.

entries.clue: Get to shag in Number ten – twice (5)

blocks.note: slang for succeeding in getting sex
twenty, reached by counting ten twice

annotation.surface: A political scandal: sex at the Prime Minister's residence, twice.
annotation.walkthrough: Number Ten is Downing Street, the PM's home, but here it is just the number 10, doubled.
annotation.definitionFit: To score is slang for landing sex; a score is twenty, two tens.

entries.clue: Mad – which shows there's something wrong (5)

blocks.note: mad in the angry sense
the mark a teacher puts beside a wrong answer

annotation.surface: Being furious is a sign that something is amiss.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mad" is angry, not insane.
annotation.definitionFit: Cross means angry, and a cross is the mark put next to an error.

entries.clue: Technique in opening of skimpy top (5)

indicatorNotes.opening of: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of skimpy
to top someone is slang for to kill them

annotation.surface: The knack of wearing a revealing low-cut top.
annotation.walkthrough: "Top" is a garment in the surface but the slang verb for murder in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Skill is technique, expertise at doing something.

entries.clue: Crack: "F— the police!" (4)

blocks.note: the letter left before the dash
the law is slang for the police

annotation.surface: A rude anti-police slogan, bleeped.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash does the work: only the F of the expletive survives.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a crack in china or glass is a flaw, a defect in the material.

entries.clue: (& 9dn.) New 'tool' – sadly on which the finish is disappointing (3)

annotation.definition: on which the finish is disappointing

indicatorNotes.sadly: letters sadly placed are in a sorry order

blocks.note: NEWTOOL rearranged

annotation.surface: A sex toy that fails to satisfy at the climax.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer continues into 9 across. The phrase "to end on a low note" is what makes the definition fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Ending on a low note means finishing disappointingly, so a low note is what a disappointing finish ends on.

entries.clue: Say Republican's constrained by rampant conceit, just like Trump (10)

indicatorNotes.rampant: letters running rampant are out of control

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, say
CONCEIT rearranged
R for Republican

annotation.surface: A jibe at the vain Republican, Donald Trump.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is is: the Republican is held inside the reshuffled conceit.
annotation.definitionFit: Egocentric means self-centred, which the setter says Trump is.

entries.clue: Angry talk when doctor shafts pig  – perverse! (5)

indicatorNotes.shafts: to shaft is to penetrate, so the doctor goes inside
indicatorNotes.perverse: perverse means turned the wrong way

blocks.note: a sow is a female pig
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

annotation.walkthrough: To have words with someone is to argue, so WORDS is angry talk.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to have words with someone is to quarrel, so the plural means angry talk.

entries.clue: Going on and on about temperature, er, in back passage (7)

indicatorNotes.about: one piece placed about another goes round it
indicatorNotes.back: to go back is to go in reverse, so the passage is read from its end

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow passage
T for temperature
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: A long, hesitant complaint about heat in the rear passage.
annotation.walkthrough: "Back passage" is a coy word for the rectum; here it is a reversed lane.
annotation.definitionFit: Something eternal goes on and on without end.
